::: {#sol-reversed-n-gram-model}

To shorten the displays,
write $p(x_a, \ldots, x_b)$ for $\P(X_a = x_a, \ldots, X_b = x_b)$,
and $p(x_a \mid x_c, \ldots, x_d)$ for $\P(X_a = x_a \mid X_c = x_c, \ldots, X_d = x_d)$.
Each value's subscript says which variable takes it.

First, for each $s$ with $t + N \le s \le n$,
the condition on $X_t, \ldots, X_{s-1}$ can be cut to the $N - 1$ variables just before $X_s$:
for values with $p(x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) > 0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(x_s \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1})
&= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \, p(x_s \mid x_1, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
&= \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \, p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
&= p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}} p(x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1} \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
&= p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}).
\end{aligned}
$$

The first line is the [law of total probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-total-prob-conditional), given $X_t, \ldots, X_{s-1}$.
The second line is the [$N$-gram model](#def-n-gram-model),
which applies
because $s > N$.
The third line takes the factor that does not depend on $x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1}$ out of the sum.
The fourth line uses that a [conditional probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cond-pmf) sums to $1$.
Because $s - N + 1 \ge t + 1$,
the same holds with $t + 1$ in place of $t$.

Write $R$ for the product of these factors:

$$R = \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_{s-N+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}).$$

The product is empty, and $R$ is $1$,
when $n = t + N - 1$.
No factor involves $x_t$,
because each starts at $x_{s-N+1}$ with $s - N + 1 \ge t + 1$.
Applying the [multiplication rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#thm-law-conditional-prob) once for each $s$ from $t + N$ to $n$,
and then the cut above to each factor,
gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(x_t, \ldots, x_n)
&= p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_t, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
&= p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R.
\end{aligned}
$$

The same two steps, starting from $x_{t+1}$, give

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)
&= p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \prod_{s=t+N}^{n} p(x_s \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{s-1}) \\
&= p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R.
\end{aligned}
$$

The left side of the second display is positive by assumption,
so $R > 0$ and $p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) > 0$.
By the definition of [conditional probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-conditional-prob),

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(x_t \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)
&= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_n)}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_n)} \\
&= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}) \, R} \\
&= \frac{p(x_t, \ldots, x_{t+N-1})}{p(x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1})} \\
&= p(x_t \mid x_{t+1}, \ldots, x_{t+N-1}).
\end{aligned}
$$

The second line substitutes the two displays above,
the third cancels $R$,
and the fourth is the definition of conditional probability again.

:::
